title: Southeast Asia's Extremes: Singapore's Mandatory Death Penalty, the Golden Triangle's Ya Ba Flood, the Philippines' Tokhang & Thailand's 2022–2026 Cannabis Rollercoaster — One-Ångström walks inside μOR–Gi1 + mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (7T2G), DAT + methamphetamine (4XP6), and human CB1 + AM11542 (5XRA); Singapore's 1973 MDA presumptions & Section 33B; UNODC's 190–236 ton Shan State ya ba math; Duterte's 2025–2026 ICC trial in The Hague; Malaysia's 2023 mandatory-death-penalty abolition & MMT/NSEP; and Thailand's PT33 medical-only cannabis reset

teenKit.tldr: Within a two-hour flight, Southeast Asia crams four radically opposite drug-policy extremes—from Singapore's mandatory death penalty to the Golden Triangle's industrial methamphetamine labs and Thailand's legal cannabis rollercoaster.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how different countries handle mind-altering substances reveals how geography, law, and molecular biology collide to shape human survival and social justice.
keyTakeaways: Singapore maintains an unyielding fortress of absolute deterrence, utilizing strict statutory presumptions, airport urine testing, and mandatory capital punishment for drug trafficking.
The Golden Triangle operates as a stateless sovereign vacuum where industrial-scale super-labs churn out tens of billions of synthetic methamphetamine pills annually.
Molecular biology shows how specific drugs lock into human brain receptors—like methamphetamine binding to the dopamine transporter or kratom variants interacting with opioid receptors.
